statement_record.book: Exercise 4.32 asks for a proof of Lemma 4.31: for V-profunctors Phi : P -|-> Q, Psi : Q -|-> R, Upsilon : R -|-> S over a SKELETAL quantale V, serial composition is associative on the nose, (Phi ; Psi) ; Upsilon = Phi ; (Psi ; Upsilon). statement_record.book: Prof_V was constructed (Thm 4.23) only for SKELETAL quantales; a non-skeletal V can be accommodated in either of two standard ways: (i) take the morphisms of Prof_V to be ISOMORPHISM CLASSES of V-profunctors — the same device used for Cospan_C in Definition 6.45 — or (ii) relax the notion of category so that composition is unital and associative only UP TO ISOMORPHISM, i.e. pass to bicategory theory, itself a form of categorification.
statement_record.intree: Both devices exist in-tree in general form but neither is applied to profunctors. Device (ii) is realized concretely for profunctors WITHOUT the bicategory packaging: prof_unit_left_iso / prof_unit_right_iso / prof_assoc_iso give the unit and associativity laws of profunctor composition as natural isomorphisms ≅[Fun]. Device (i) is realized at the remark's own cited example: CospanCat : Category, whose hom-setoid identifies cospans up to isomorphism of apexes, so that 'relative to that ≈ the unit and associativity laws hold strictly' (file header). Device (ii) as a named notion is Class Bicategory, with hunit_left/hunit_right/hassoc recorded as 2-isomorphisms in the hom-categories and constrained by triangle + pentagon.

Record Companion {a b : dcat} (u : a ~> b) : Type := { comp_hor : dhor a b; comp_unit : dsq (dhid a) id u comp_hor; comp_counit : dsq comp_hor u id (dhid b); comp_zig : dsq_coerce (id_left id) (id_left id) (dsq_vcomp (dunit_right_to comp_hor) (dunit_left_from comp_hor)) ≈ dsq_hcomp comp_unit comp_counit; comp_zag_eval : ∀ h' e, companion_eval u comp_hor comp_counit (companion_name u comp_hor comp_unit e) ≈ e; comp_zag_name : ∀ h' g, companion_name u comp_hor comp_unit (companion_eval u comp_hor comp_counit g) ≈ g }.

Record Conjoint {a b : dcat} (u : a ~> b) : Type := { conj_hor : dhor b a; conj_unit : dsq (dhid a) u id conj_hor; conj_counit : dsq conj_hor id u (dhid b); conj_zig : ...; conj_zag_eval : ...; conj_zag_name : ... }.  (note the direction: conj_hor runs b to a, matching the book's F-check : Q -|-> P)

statement_record.book: For a V-functor F : P -> Q, the COMPANION is the V-profunctor F-hat : P -|-> Q with F-hat(p,q) := Q(F p, q), and the CONJOINT is the V-profunctor F-check : Q -|-> P with F-check(q,p) := Q(q, F p).
statement_record.intree: Repr_left F := Hom D ◯ (F^op ∏⟶ Id) : C ⇸ D, i.e. (c,d) ↦ D(F c, d), and Repr_right U := Hom C ◯ (Id^op ∏⟶ U) : C ⇸ D, i.e. (c,d) ↦ C(c, U d), which at U := F reads (q,p) ↦ Q(q, F p). Abstractly, the double-category records Companion u / Conjoint u package the same notion as a horizontal 1-cell equipped with binding squares satisfying the horizontal zigzag and the representability (name/eval) transposition.

evidence.intree_statement: Class Adjunction := { adj {x y} : @Isomorphism Sets {| carrier := @hom C (F x) y; is_setoid := @homset C (F x) y |} {| carrier := @hom D x (U y); is_setoid := @homset D x (U y) |} where "⌊ f ⌋" := (to adj f) and "⌈ f ⌉" := (from adj f); to_adj_nat_l {x y z} (f : F y ~> z) (g : x ~> y) : ⌊f ∘ fmap[F] g⌋ ≈ ⌊f⌋ ∘ g; to_adj_nat_r {x y z} (f : y ~> z) (g : F x ~> y) : ⌊f ∘ g⌋ ≈ fmap[U] f ∘ ⌊g⌋; ... }.
Class Adjunction_Hom := { hom_adj : Hom C ◯ F^op ∏⟶ Id ≅[[D^op ∏ C, Sets]] Hom D ◯ Id^op ∏⟶ U }.

Program Definition Proset {A : Type} {R : relation A} (P : PreOrder R) : Category := {| obj := A; hom := R; homset := fun A B => {| Setoid.equiv := fun _ _ => True |}; id := fun x => reflexivity x; compose := fun x y z f g => transitivity g f |}.  (a preorder AS a category, so an Adjunction between two Prosets is exactly a Galois connection — the Bool case the remark generalizes)

statement_record.book: Generalizing Galois connections (Def 1.95, the Bool-enriched case), a V-ADJUNCTION for a monoidal preorder V is a pair of V-functors F : P -> Q and G : Q -> P such that P(p, G q) ≅ Q(F p, q) for all p, q (display 4.40); when V is skeletal the isomorphism is an equality of hom-objects.
statement_record.intree: The hom-object form exists only at V = Sets: Class Adjunction's field adj is an isomorphism in Sets between the hom-setoids C(F x, y) and D(x, U y), with naturality in both variables recorded as the four fields to_adj_nat_l / to_adj_nat_r / from_adj_nat_l / from_adj_nat_r; and Adjunction_Hom's field hom_adj states the same thing as a natural isomorphism of the two hom-bifunctors in [D^op ∏ C, Sets]. The Bool instance is available indirectly because Proset makes a preorder a thin category, so an Adjunction between Prosets is a Galois connection (as Instance/Poset.v:47 and Theory/Adjunction.v:78 both note in prose).
statement_record.strength_comparison: intree-weaker in the enrichment base only. The library has Enriched (over any monoidal K, with ehom : eobj → eobj → K) and EnrichedFunctor, so V-categories and V-functors ARE in-tree for a general base — but there is no enriched adjunction: a search for any V-level isomorphism ehom-to-ehom returns nothing. Consequently display (4.40) can be stated only for K = Sets, where 'isomorphism of hom-objects' is an isomorphism of hom-SETOIDS. In one respect the in-tree class is stronger than the remark: it demands naturality of the transposition explicitly, whereas the remark leaves it implicit (harmless for a quantale base, where hom-objects are elements of a preorder and naturality is automatic).

gap: There is no V-adjunction over a general monoidal/quantale base: nothing in Construction/Enriched.v or its satellites states P(p, G q) ≅ Q(F p, q) at the level of ehom, and no class pairs two EnrichedFunctors adjointly. What exists is the V = Sets case (Adjunction.adj, Adjunction_Hom.hom_adj) and, via Proset, the V = Bool case realized as an ordinary adjunction between thin categories rather than as an enriched notion. The skeletal upgrade of the isomorphism to an equality of hom-objects has no in-tree counterpart.

statement_record.book: Let V be a skeletal quantale, P and Q V-categories and F : P -> Q, G : Q -> P V-functors. (1) F and G are V-adjoints in the sense of (4.40) iff the companion of F equals the conjoint of G, F-hat = G-check. (2) Deduce id-hat = id-check, as asserted in Example 4.35.
statement_record.intree: representable_adjunction : (F ⊣ U) ↔ (Repr_left F ≅[[D^op ∏ C, Sets]] Repr_right U) — an iff, with both directions constructed (adjunction_to_repr_iso routes an adjunction through Adjunction_Universal_to_Hom to the hom-bifunctor iso hom_adj, whose endpoints are definitionally Repr_left F and Repr_right U; repr_iso_to_adjunction reads such an iso back as an Adjunction_Hom and converts it by Adjunction_Hom_to_Universal). Clause (2) is one application away via adj_id : Id ⊣ Id but is not stated.
statement_record.strength_comparison: Clause (1) matches the book almost exactly, and at full biconditional strength — this is the closest in-tree match of any item in this batch. The differences are base and strictness: (a) V = Sets rather than a skeletal quantale, since the library has no quantale and no V-profunctors, so 'companion' and 'conjoint' here mean Repr_left / Repr_right for ordinary categories; (b) the conclusion is a natural ISOMORPHISM in [D^op ∏ C, Sets] rather than the strict equality skeletality delivers — which is the correct notion at V = Sets but strictly weaker than what the exercise asks for. Clause (2) is absent as a statement.

gap: Clause (1) is present at V = Sets as a genuine biconditional but not over a skeletal quantale, and its conclusion is an iso rather than an equality. Clause (2) — id-hat = id-check — is never recorded, though it follows in one step from representable_adjunction applied to adj_id; and its further identification with the unit profunctor U_P (Example 4.35) is likewise unstated.
